rewriteLast.title: Chapter 6 · Out of the Underground
rewriteLast.artPrompt: a long rocky passage climbing toward a bright doorway of daylight, a fairy princess in a green crown leading a line of freed prisoners up worn stone steps, a girl in a blue dress with a yellow hen on her shoulder and a copper man behind, warm sun spilling down into the darkness, hopeful storybook illustration

blocks.text: At last it was time to leave the Nome King’s kingdom. Ozma led the way, and the Queen of Ev walked beside her with her children close around her. The passage climbed and climbed, up and up through the dark rock. Tik-Tok clanked along behind, careful and slow. Dorothy held on to Ozma’s hand, so as not to trip in the dark. Billina rode proudly on Dorothy’s shoulder, like a small yellow captain. Step by step the daylight came nearer, until it poured down the stairs like warm honey. No one looked back at the dark.
The friends climb the long passage back up to daylight.
New word: passage — a long, narrow way through rock or between walls. This one led all the way from the Nome King’s dark caverns up into the sun.

At the top, the friends stepped out into golden sunshine. The palace of Ev stood near, with its gardens, its fountains, and its flags. The people of Ev cheered when they saw their royal family come home at last. Everyone hugged everyone at once, and Ozma waited politely before she could pass. Banners waved from every tower in the old walls. Tik-Tok had to be wound up twice, because he kept stopping to think about the wonderful day. Dorothy looked up at the blue sky and took a deep, deep breath. There is no air in the world as sweet as air after a cave.

That evening there was a happy supper in the palace of Ev. Dorothy sat between Ozma and Tik-Tok, and Billina pecked crumbs from her plate, tired and pleased. The Queen of Ev thanked Dorothy so many times that Dorothy grew pink all over. “Tomorrow,” said Ozma, “we shall crown a new King for this land. And then, Dorothy, you must come away with me — for I have something wonderful to show you.” Dorothy’s eyes grew round as buttons. “More wonderful than a cavern full of ornaments?” she asked. “Much more,” said Ozma, and smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 · A New King and a Magic Carpet
chapters.artPrompt: a wide glowing carpet unrolling itself across golden desert sands like a bright ribbon, a fairy princess riding a wooden sawhorse upon it while a girl in a blue dress walks beside, a copper man and a yellow hen following, a green shore far ahead, bright open sky, adventurous storybook illustration

blocks.text: In the morning, trumpets sounded through the palace of Ev. The Queen’s eldest son was crowned King, and all the people shouted for joy. The Queen wore her silver gown and could not stop smiling. The young King came to Dorothy first of all. “You brought my family back to me,” he said, bowing very low. “Ask anything you like in Ev, and it is yours.” Dorothy could not think of anything she wanted. She had her friends, her yellow hen, and — she patted it — a very fine magic belt. Then the new King wished them good luck on their journey.

Then Ozma took Dorothy’s hand. “Now come with me to the Emerald City of Oz,” she said. “You shall be my guest, and Billina too, and Tik-Tok, if he wishes.” “I wish it ver-y much,” said Tik-Tok, in his slow, clicking way. Billina flew up onto Dorothy’s shoulder at once, for a clever hen never misses a chance. Saved from the sea one week, invited to fairyland the next — Dorothy could hardly believe her luck. Ozma unrolled her magic carpet, and it spread itself over the Deadly Desert like a bright ribbon.
The magic carpet carries them safely across the Deadly Desert.
New word: desert — a land so dry that hardly anything grows there. The Deadly Desert around Oz was the deadliest of all, so a magic carpet was much safer than walking.

They walked on the soft carpet all day long, and the hot sands never once touched their feet. Ozma rode her wooden Sawhorse, trotting politely beside them. Tik-Tok marched with his keys turning, and Billina saw everything from the best perch. Far ahead, a green shore came nearer and nearer. “That is Oz,” said Ozma, “the land where nobody is ever unhappy.” By evening they reached the meadows, and the gates of the Emerald City opened with music. There, shining like a jewel box left open in the sun, stood every tower and roof. “It is the most beautiful thing I ever saw,” said Dorothy.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 · Welcome to the Emerald City
chapters.artPrompt: a grand banquet hall of green marble with emerald chandeliers, a fairy princess and a girl in a blue dress at a long sparkling table, a scarecrow, a tin woodman, a lion and a striped tiger bowing in welcome, festive warm light, joyful storybook illustration

blocks.text: The green gates of the Emerald City opened wide, and everyone came out to cheer. Music played, flags flew, and the streets were paved with polished green marble. Dorothy had never seen so many happy people in one place. “Welcome home, Princess Ozma!” they called. “Welcome, Dorothy of Oz!” Dorothy wondered when she had become Dorothy of Oz — and decided she liked the sound of it very much.
Ozma’s friends greet Dorothy at a grand welcome feast.

In the great hall, Ozma presented her dearest friends. There was the Scarecrow, wise and kind, though he was only stuffed with straw. There was the Tin Woodman, so gentle that he seemed to shine. There was the Cowardly Lion, big and soft, and brave whenever it mattered. And there was the Hungry Tiger, whose tummy rumbled like thunder though his manners were perfect. Each of them bowed to Dorothy in turn, and Billina clucked a polite hello.
New word: present — to introduce someone in a formal, careful way. Ozma presented her friends one by one, and each bowed lower than the last.

That night there was a feast of every good thing you can think of, and a great many you cannot. Afterward, Dorothy was shown to her very own room in the palace. It had a soft bed, a little balcony, and a window full of stars. “Tomorrow we shall play,” said Ozma. “I shall show you the whole city, and the Sawhorse shall carry you.” Dorothy fell asleep smiling, with Billina dreaming on the post of her bed.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 · Rides on the Sawhorse
chapters.artPrompt: a wooden sawhorse with jointed wooden legs trotting in mid-gallop down an emerald city street, a girl in a blue dress laughing on its back, a fairy princess walking beside, jewelled houses and fountains passing by, bright sparkling daylight, merry storybook illustration

blocks.text:
Every day in the Emerald City brought something new. Dorothy visited the fountains, the gardens, and the shops where everything glittered green and gold. But best of all was the Sawhorse — a wooden horse with wooden legs that never, ever grew tired. It could gallop all day without stopping once for hay or water. “It is the most sensible horse in the world,” said Dorothy. The Sawhorse turned its log head and nodded.

Then Ozma called for a ride, and off they went. The Sawhorse sped down the emerald streets like the wind. Dorothy held tight and laughed with the wind in her hair. People came to their doors and waved as she passed. Fountains flashed, gardens blazed, and the whole city sparkled. “Faster!” cried Dorothy. And the kind wooden horse ran faster still, smooth as a boat on calm water.
Dorothy rides the wooden Sawhorse through the city.
New word: gallop — the fastest way for a horse to run. The Sawhorse galloped so fast that its wooden legs were only a blur.

Each morning, Dorothy and Ozma wound up Tik-Tok’s three keys together. Then his copper clockwork went clatter-click-clack through the palace all day long. He guarded the gates, told the time, and spoke so slowly that Dorothy learned to wait patiently for his words.

His three keys were famous all over the palace. One key made him think. One made him speak. The third made his arms and legs move, slow and steady. When they were wound just right, Tik-Tok walked, talked, and thought all together. When they ran down, he stopped in the middle of a word. Dorothy grew very good at winding them, morning by morning.

“I — am — ver-y — hap-py — here,” he told her one evening. Dorothy laughed until she had to sit down on the palace steps. “So am I, Tik-Tok,” she said. “So am I.”

chapters.title: Chapter 10 · Billina’s Chicks
chapters.artPrompt: a plump yellow hen proudly sitting in a cosy nest of straw in a sunny palace garden, a row of tiny fluffy chicks peeping out beneath her wing, a girl in a blue dress kneeling to look, emerald grass and flowers around, tender storybook illustration

blocks.text: One morning, Billina was missing. Dorothy searched the whole palace, calling her name through every room and corridor. At last she heard a soft, proud cluck coming from the garden. There sat Billina on a cosy nest of straw, with her feathers all puffed out. “Do not disturb me, please,” said Billina. “I am hatching eggs — and I shall never tell what is inside them.”

“Why not?” asked Dorothy. “Because a hen never tells,” said Billina, and turned back to her eggs. Dorothy tiptoed away and told Ozma, and Ozma smiled her wisest smile. Every day after that, they brought Billina the finest seeds and the softest straw. And every day, Billina sat a little straighter and looked a little prouder. Something wonderful was clearly on the way.
Billina hatches her eggs in the sunny palace garden.
New word: hatch — to break out of an egg, or to keep eggs warm until they do. A mother hen sits very patiently until her chicks hatch.

A few days later, the shells began to crack. Out peeped a whole row of tiny, fluffy chicks. Dorothy clapped her hands with joy, and Ozma came running to see. “You clever hen!” cried Dorothy. Billina looked as pleased as any mother in the world. The chicks peeped and tumbled about the garden all day long, and Ozma said they might stay in Oz forever. “I shall never tell how I did it,” said Billina. “A hen must keep some secrets.”

chapters.title: Chapter 11 · Thinking of Home
chapters.artPrompt: a fairy princess drawing back a small curtain on a tall framed picture that glows like a bright window, a small Kansas farm and an older man in a broad hat visible inside the frame, a girl in a blue dress watching with misty eyes, a yellow hen nestled close, soft green-gold light, gentle storybook illustration

blocks.text: Dorothy was happy in Oz — but one evening she grew very quiet. She sat by the window, thinking of Uncle Henry far away in Kansas. He did not know where she was, or even if she was alive. Her eyes filled with tears, and Billina nestled close against her. Ozma came into the room and saw the tears at once. “You are thinking of home,” she said gently.

“Do not be sad,” said Ozma. “Come and see my Magic Picture.” She drew back a little curtain, and the frame glowed like a window. Inside it, Dorothy saw the Kansas farm, plain and grey and dear. Uncle Henry stood looking down the road, hoping for Dorothy’s return. “Oh!” cried Dorothy. “He is safe — but he misses me dreadfully.”
The Magic Picture shows Dorothy her Uncle Henry in Kansas.
New word: curtain — a hanging cloth that covers a window or door. This little curtain hid a picture that could show any place in the world.

“Then you must go to him,” said Ozma kindly. “Your magic belt will take you home in the wink of an eye.” Dorothy looked up quickly. “And can I come back?” “Whenever you wish,” said Ozma. “Tomorrow, next year, or any day at all. Oz will always be here, and so will I.” Dorothy dried her eyes and hugged her friend as tight as she could. “Then I am not sad anymore,” she said. “I am only going to visit.”

chapters.title: Chapter 12 · Good-bye, Oz
chapters.artPrompt: a girl in a blue dress hugging a fairy princess at shining green gates, a scarecrow, a tin woodman and a lion waving behind, a copper man standing straight and tall, a yellow hen with a row of chicks beside her, soft morning light with green sparkles, tender storybook illustration

blocks.text: The next morning, all of Dorothy’s friends came to say good-bye. The Scarecrow gave her his very best piece of advice. The Tin Woodman polished a bright tear from his tin cheek. The Cowardly Lion gave her a soft, furry hug that nearly squeezed the breath out of her. Even the Hungry Tiger came, purring like a very large kitten. “Good-bye, Dorothy of Oz,” they said, one by one.

Billina stayed in the Emerald City to look after her chicks. “You will be happiest here,” said Dorothy, and Billina agreed with a happy cluck. Tik-Tok shook her hand so slowly that it took a whole minute. Then Ozma held Dorothy’s hands in her own. “Wherever you are,” she said, “you will always be my friend, and Oz will always be your second home.”
Dorothy says good-bye at the gates of the Emerald City.
New word: farewell — a kind word said when someone leaves. A farewell can be sad and glad at the very same time.

Ozma touched the magic belt, and the air began to sparkle. “Good-bye, Dorothy!” everyone called. “Come back soon!” The green light swirled round and round like a wheel of stars. The last thing Dorothy saw was Ozma smiling and waving. Then the sparkles wrapped her round, and the fairyland she loved grew small and bright, like a faraway lantern in the dark.

chapters.title: Chapter 13 · Home Again in Kansas
chapters.artPrompt: a sunny Kansas farmyard with a wooden fence and a windmill, an older man in a broad hat lifting a girl in a blue dress into the air with joy, her small suitcase on the grass, wide prairie sky with soft clouds, warm golden light, heartwarming storybook illustration

blocks.text: There was a whirl of green light — and then Dorothy stood on the dry grass of the Kansas farm. The prairie wind blew in her hair, and the little grey house looked exactly as she had left it. For one moment she almost missed the emeralds. Then a door banged, and a well-known voice shouted her name. Dorothy turned and began to run.

Uncle Henry came running from the barn faster than he had run in twenty years. “Dorothy!” he cried. “We thought you were lost at sea!” “I was,” said Dorothy, “more or less. But I made the very best friends in the world, and I found my way home again.” Uncle Henry lifted her right off the ground and would not put her down. The windmill creaked above them, and the sky was wide and kind.
Uncle Henry runs across the farmyard to meet Dorothy.
New word: prairie — a wide, flat land covered with grass, like a sea of green. Dorothy’s prairie looked very small next to the real sea she had crossed.

That evening Dorothy told him everything. She told him about Billina and the floating coop, Tik-Tok and his three keys, the Wheelers, the princess with the cabinet of heads, and the Nome King in his cavern. Uncle Henry listened with his mouth open. “And the best part,” said Dorothy, touching the magic belt at her waist, “is that I can go back to Oz whenever I wish.” She smiled up at the first stars. And she always did.
